stories.title: The Lion Roars
stories.keyVerse: "The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?"
stories.retelling:
Amos, a humble herdsman from the small town of Tekoa, stood amidst the vast plains, his eyes scanning the horizon. It was a time when Israel thrived under King Jeroboam, yet the air was thick with foreboding. The ground beneath his feet seemed to pulse with a warning known only to him. Two years before a great earthquake would shake the land, Amos was stirred by a vision, a divine message that would change everything.

As the sun dipped behind the mountains, casting long, dark shadows, Amos felt a surge of something powerful—a presence that commanded attention. The voice he heard wasn’t just in his ears; it resonated in his bones, as if the very earth was speaking. It was the voice of Yahweh, echoing through the valleys and over the hills, a roar from Zion itself. **“The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.”**

Amos's heart pounded as he pictured the devastation foretold. The once vibrant pastures where shepherds tended their flocks would be shrouded in mourning. The majestic Carmel, known for its lush greenery, would stand withered and barren. The roar signaled not just destruction but a call to attention—a cosmic summons that no one could ignore.

In his mind's eye, Amos saw the fate of nations unfold like a tapestry of fire and ruin. Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, and Edom—all had sinned grievously. Their trespasses were etched into the heavens: Damascus had threshed Gilead with iron instruments; Gaza had captured entire communities to be sold in Edom. Each nation was marked for judgment, and Amos could see the flames licking at the palaces of kings, reducing their grandeur to ash.

Yahweh's message was relentless, spreading like wildfire through Amos's consciousness. The children of Ammon, Moab, and even his own people, Judah and Israel, were not spared. Their transgressions were laid bare: the rejection of divine laws, oppression of the righteous, and profaning of the sacred. The visions were stark and unyielding, much like the fierce winds that swept through the desert landscapes.

Yet, amid the impending doom, there was a plea—a whisper of hope. **“Seek me, and ye shall live,”** the voice urged, a beacon in the gathering darkness. Amos knew the truth of these words; it was a call to turn back, to restore what was broken.

As the lion’s roar echoed in his memory, Amos understood his role. He was to be the voice crying out, the prophet who could not keep silent. The roar was a call to fear and a call to speak. The world around him might crumble, but the message of Yahweh would stand, unwavering. In that moment, standing alone yet emboldened by the divine, Amos knew that he must prophesy.
